Nibiru 01702231 (Ensemble Inegal/Viktora) opens with the 'Sonata a 8', the one instrumental work certainly by Capricornus (MusicWeb review); 6:50. Key not stated on the album. IMSLP/Wikipedia scoring: 3 vn, 2 va da braccio, 2 viols, viola di basso, continuo (Duben ms 1667); 'a 8' counts the 8 concertante parts, so 9 players is right.

Op. 21 in IMSLP and fr/de Wikipedia; Harp & Co CD plays it one to a part (harp, 2 vn, va, vc), 13:55. IMSLP's 'ca. 1775' looks wrong (Op. 21 postdates his Op. 19, issued as J.-B. Cardon), so the blank year is right.

Harp & Co CD titles them 'Trio for harp, violin and viola, Op. 9' (Apple and Deezer, 17:23 and 17:29, two movements each, matches the entry). But no catalogue confirms Op. 9: fr/de Wikipedia list only '2 Trios (1790)' with no opus, and the same CD's sonatas are Op. 10 where Wikipedia has Op. 11; a bookseller lists Cardon's oeuvre 9 as harp sonatas. Recorded, so they stay; the opus number and the set name rest on one CD booklet (title could become 'Trio for Harp, Violin and Viola No. 1', year 1790?).

note: Cambini, Campagnoli, Campioni, Campos, Capricornus, Caro, Campa: all recorded and described correctly; fixes are small (years, aka, durations fine). Carolo: the print names two viols (or bassoons or basses de violon), not cellos, so all nine are fixed to viola-da-gamba with alternatives; Carolo's No. 3 (G minor) is absent and appears on the Leaf recording only as an arrangement. Cardon trios: Op. 9 unconfirmed. Meneleu Campos's A-major quartet (106076, not in this chunk) is No. 2 (1899) per Rev. Tulha 2021.
